_meta.description: Canonical friend database for the Bella content engine. v2.0 supersedes the SEO/GBP premise: friends are framed around missed calls, after-hours bookings, no-shows, OpenTable cover fees, the language gap, and the Quandoo exit. All before/after arcs and enemy archetypes reframed to calls & bookings (premise-pivot-v2). Active roster is 60% Australian / 40% international (see top-level `roster`).

before_bella.personal: Left work after midnight every Tuesday. Stopped answering calls from her sister in Boston — she of all people knew what an unanswered call costs.

after_bella.operational: Every call answered, even mid-service. The after-hours enquiries that used to be gone by morning now land in the book overnight.
after_bella.personal: Left work before midnight on a Tuesday for the first time in two years.

before_bella.operational: Maria takes booking enquiries on her mobile at 11pm because the line can't; the after-hours calls that don't reach her are gone by morning. And the OpenTable cover fees — base plus per-cover plus service — bleed a four-generation family margin every month.
before_bella.personal: Enzo and Maria argued more than they talked. The stress was in the kitchen and at home.

after_bella.operational: A line that takes the after-hours bookings while they sleep, paired with a commission-free booking system instead of the OpenTable invoice. The 11pm enquiries land in the book, not on Maria's mobile.
after_bella.personal: Son Luca (8) came in for a Saturday lunch at the chef's table. Enzo talked about it for a week.

operational: 10:48pm, Maria taking a King's Birthday lunch booking on her mobile again — the calls she misses after close are gone by morning.
The OpenTable invoice on the pass: base, per-cover, service fee, every month — eating a margin four generations built. A flat commission-free line would cost a fraction.
Easter long weekend: the after-hours enquiries flood in for the special menu Enzo's grandfather wrote in 1968, and the line can't take them while the family is on the floor.
personal: Enzo and Maria argued more than they talked. The stress was in the kitchen and at home.
Their son Luca grew used to them not being at school events. The week he came in for a chef's table lunch, Enzo talked about it for a week — like he'd just met him.
A fourth-generation restaurant felt heavier than they admitted. The grandfather's photograph above the till had stopped being a comfort and become a question.

friends.personality: Enzo's laugh fills the whole trattoria — he can find a reason to celebrate in any night. Maria's quieter warmth is the glue; she asks the question no one else thought to ask, always with a small smile. Together they make every friend who walks in feel like family within thirty seconds. Finish each other's sentences without noticing.

after_bella.personal: Linh's parents still answer the phone when they want to. But the line never goes to voicemail in the wrong language anymore — and the Saturday Tết bookings start coming in three weeks earlier.

operational: Lunch rush — phone rings while her parents can't take English bookings; the office crowd gives up.

personal: Mẹ never let Linh change the laminated specials board; the family's name on the door is what they protect most.
Linh runs front-and-kitchen at once — code-switching between English and Vietnamese mid-sentence, fiercely protective of her parents.

friends.story_angle: A family Greek taverna stranded on Quandoo as the platform shuts down — needing a replacement booking line that answers in Greek before the Glendi rush

before_bella.operational: Stranded on Quandoo as it shuts down, and missing after-hours calls during the Greek-community dinner trade — Yiayia answering in Greek while the English bookings ring out.
before_bella.personal: Kostas keeps the Quandoo shutdown email in his apron pocket like a parking ticket. Yiayia hasn't seen it. He doesn't want her to think the family business is the one being switched off.

after_bella.operational: Migrated to a commission-free line that answers in Greek and English. The Saturday glendi books itself; Kostas is back on the floor pouring wine instead of chasing the phone.
after_bella.personal: Yiayia keeps answering the regulars in Greek. The line takes the rest. The family name stays on the door — and the door stays open.

operational: Greek Orthodox Easter — the single biggest booking week of the year; after-hours demand floods in and the calls ring out.

personal: Yiayia is the real boss and Kostas knows it; his job is to make sure the phyllo, not the platform, is what decides Saturday.
Kostas remembers every regular's order; the worry beads come out when the phone doesn't.

friends.personality: Big, warm, loud laugh — feeds everyone, remembers every regular's order. Proud of the family name. Yiayia is the real boss and he knows it.
